[LCSP.4.1] **Validation subset.** The compiler runs the same
bounded-memory validation pass as `realtime` on `constspace`
programs. This covers the LNLS.3 subset that gates against
unbounded allocation:

- LNLS.3.2 — novel strings a rule PRODUCES (an interpolated string).
  Note this does not lock the intern table under `constspace`, which
  has no phase boundary to lock at ([LCSP.3.5]); strings arriving on
  asserted facts are a different population and are not gated.
- LNLS.3.5 — sketch backends (v1 ships none)
- LNLS.3.7 — `regex` without `capacity`
- LNLS.3.8 — string ordering in cross-pattern position
- LNLS.3.9 — `JSON_PATH` (unbounded allocation)
- LNLS.3.11 — series scan without a sample cap

The same constraints apply for the same reason: each violates
"steady-state allocation is zero" if permitted at pump time. The
reference compiler reuses `_check_realtime` for `constspace`.

**This subset is not the whole of the `constspace` check.**
`linear_scan: false` excludes features for their *algorithmic shape*, and the
overlap with bounded memory is real but partial: an obligation that is
purely about allocation has no `LNLS.3` clause to correspond to,
because a per-sample copy is O(1) and `linear_scan: false` has no objection to
it. [LCSP.4.5] is such an obligation, and a validator that runs only
the list above misses it.
